title: Beef Rendang
subtitle: Slow-cooked beef in spiced coconut milk
excerpt: Beef chuck simmered in spiced coconut milk until the liquid has almost completely reduced, leaving the meat tender, dark, and coated in a fragrant paste. This is a dish where patience is the main skill.
sourceNotes: Rendang originates with the Minangkabau people of West Sumatra, Indonesia, where it has been prepared for centuries. Traditionally cooked in large quantities for celebrations and festivals, the dry-style cooking method was also a preservation technique in the hot climate, allowing the dish to last for weeks.

recipe.freezeNotes: Cool fully before freezing. Reheat gently on the hob with a splash of water.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Rendang tastes better the next day and keeps well in the fridge for 4 days.

content.text: The final stage of rendang, when the coconut milk has reduced and the beef fries in the residual fat, is what gives it the dark coating and deep flavour. Stay close at this point and stir often to prevent burning.

items.prepNote: 4 cm piece, peeled and finely grated

content.text: Heat the oil in the stockpot over medium heat. Fry the onions for 8 minutes until soft. Add the garlic, ginger, and curry paste and cook for 3 minutes, stirring constantly.
Add the ground spices and cook for 1 minute. Add the beef and stir to coat in the paste.

Pour in the coconut milk and add the kaffir lime leaves. Bring to a simmer, then cook uncovered over medium-low heat for 1 hour 30 minutes, stirring occasionally. The liquid will reduce significantly.
Once the liquid has nearly all gone and the beef is frying in a thick paste, stir continuously for 10 to 15 minutes until the coating is dark and fragrant. The beef should be very tender.
Remove the kaffir lime leaves. Season with salt to taste and serve with steamed rice.

items.symptom: Beef is dry rather than tender
items.cause: Heat was too high or cooked too fast
items.fix: Keep heat low and low. Give it more time.

items.cause: Left unattended during the final frying stage
items.fix: Stir every minute once the liquid is gone.
Add an extra tablespoon of curry paste at the start.
